steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

#!/bin/bash
# GRPO + LoRA (merged into the rollout weights) on GSM8K with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, verl FSDP2 + vLLM.
# Follows verl's examples/tuning/lora/run_qwen3_8b_merge_fsdp.sh, sized for one GPU.
# Extra Hydra overrides given on the command line are appended last and take precedence.
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

MODEL=${MODEL:-$WS/models/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct}
DATA=${DATA:-$WS/data}
TRAIN_FILES=${TRAIN_FILES:-$DATA/gsm8k/train.parquet}
VAL_FILES=${VAL_FILES:-$DATA/gsm8k/test.parquet}
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-1}
TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-60}
TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-5}
BATCH=${BATCH:-128}
N_SAMPLES=${N_SAMPLES:-8}
MAX_RESPONSE=${MAX_RESPONSE:-1024}
LR=${LR:-3e-5}
LORA_RANK=${LORA_RANK:-32}
LORA_ALPHA=${LORA_ALPHA:-64}
SEED=${SEED:-1}
EXP=${EXP:-qwen25_1.5b_gsm8k_grpo_lora_merge}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$WS/outputs}

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$WS/verl${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline} WANDB_DIR="$LOG_DIR"
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="$TRAIN_FILES" \
  data.val_files="$VAL_FILES" \
  data.train_batch_size=$BATCH \
  data.max_prompt_length=512 \
  data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=$SEED \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=$LORA_RANK \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=$LORA_ALPHA \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy=fsdp2 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.model_dtype=bf16 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$LR \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$((BATCH / 2)) \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.6 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$N_SAMPLES \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  trainer.use_v1=False \
  trainer.critic_warmup=0 \
  trainer.logger='["console","wandb"]' \
  trainer.project_name=gsm8k_grpo_lora \
  trainer.experiment_name="$EXP" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$N_GPUS \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS \
  trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations" \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=32 \

#!/bin/bash
# GRPO + LoRA (merged into the rollout weights) on GSM8K with Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, verl FSDP2 + vLLM.
# Follows verl's examples/tuning/lora/run_qwen3_8b_merge_fsdp.sh, sized for one GPU.
# Extra Hydra overrides given on the command line are appended last and take precedence.
set -euo pipefail
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"

MODEL=${MODEL:-$WS/models/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct}
DATA=${DATA:-$WS/data}
TRAIN_FILES=${TRAIN_FILES:-$DATA/gsm8k/train.parquet}
VAL_FILES=${VAL_FILES:-$DATA/gsm8k/test.parquet}
N_GPUS=${N_GPUS:-1}
TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-60}
TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-5}
BATCH=${BATCH:-128}
N_SAMPLES=${N_SAMPLES:-8}
MAX_RESPONSE=${MAX_RESPONSE:-1024}
LR=${LR:-3e-5}
LORA_RANK=${LORA_RANK:-32}
LORA_ALPHA=${LORA_ALPHA:-64}
SEED=${SEED:-1}
EXP=${EXP:-qwen25_1.5b_gsm8k_grpo_lora_merge}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$WS/outputs}

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$WS/verl${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline} WANDB_DIR="$LOG_DIR"
export RAY_DEDUP_LOGS=0

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
  algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo \
  algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False \
  data.train_files="$TRAIN_FILES" \
  data.val_files="$VAL_FILES" \
  data.train_batch_size=$BATCH \
  data.max_prompt_length=512 \
  data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE \
  data.filter_overlong_prompts=True \
  data.truncation=error \
  data.seed=$SEED \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL" \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_rank=$LORA_RANK \
  actor_rollout_ref.model.lora_alpha=$LORA_ALPHA \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.strategy=fsdp2 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.model_dtype=bf16 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$LR \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$((BATCH / 2)) \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=0.001 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0 \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.6 \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$N_SAMPLES \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True \
  actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=49152 \
  trainer.use_v1=False \
  trainer.critic_warmup=0 \
  trainer.logger='["console","wandb"]' \
  trainer.project_name=gsm8k_grpo_lora \
  trainer.experiment_name="$EXP" \
  trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$N_GPUS \
  trainer.nnodes=1 \
  trainer.val_before_train=True \
  trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ \
  trainer.save_freq=-1 \
  trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS \
  trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints" \
  trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts" \
  trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations" \
  ray_kwargs.ray_init.num_cpus=32 \
  +ray_kwargs.ray_init.object_store_memory=21474836480 \
  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

"""
Rollout Correction Helper Module

This module provides a complete pipeline to address **off-policy issues** in RL training,
including:
1. Policy mismatch between rollout and training implementations (e.g., vLLM BFloat16 vs FSDP FP32)
2. Model update staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)
3. General distribution shifts between data collection and training

Its core capabilities include computing importance sampling (IS) weights,
filtering outlier samples via rejection sampling (RS), and
tracking metrics to diagnose and correct off-policy issues.

## Core Capabilities
1. **Multi-Granularity Aggregation**:
   - Importance Sampling (IS):
        Token-level
        Sequence-level
   - Rejection Sampling (RS):
        Divergence-based filters (token_k*, seq_sum_k*, seq_mean_k*, seq_max_k*)
2. **Memory-Efficient Design**:
   - Log-space computations to avoid numerical overflow/underflow.
   - Fixed safety bounds (exp(±20)) for stable exponentiation.
   - Metrics calculated without large intermediate tensors (prevents CUDA OOM).
3. **Comprehensive Metrics Tracking**:
   - IS/RS statistics (mean/max/min, effective sample size ESS, rejection rate).
   - Off-policy diagnostics (KL divergence, perplexity PPL, log PPL difference, χ² divergence).
   - Sequence-level breakdowns (deviation from ideal weights, outlier fraction).

## Key Interfaces & Usage
- compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(): compute IS weights + rejection mask.
- compute_rollout_correction_weights(): only compute truncated IS weights (for variance
  reduction, no outlier rejection).
- compute_rollout_rejection_mask(): only filter outliers (for sample cleaning, no IS weight
  computation).
- compute_offpolicy_metrics(): called by core functions to calculate off-policy diagnostics
  (KL/PPL/χ²) — no direct external calls needed.

### Integration Notes
- Used in `ray_trainer.py` via `compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch()` (batch training pipeline).
- Used in `dp_actor.py` for distributed worker computations (distributed training scenarios).
- All functions support batch inputs and valid token masking (via `response_mask`).


## References
- "When Speed Kills Stability: Demystifying RL Collapse from the Training-Inference Mismatch": https://richardli.xyz/rl-collapse
- Off-policy RL (theoretical basis for IS): https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl

Rollout Correction Helper Module

This module provides a complete pipeline to address **off-policy issues** in RL training,
including:
1. Policy mismatch between rollout and training implementations (e.g., vLLM BFloat16 vs FSDP FP32)
2. Model update staleness (training on trajectories from older checkpoints)
3. General distribution shifts between data collection and training

Its core capabilities include computing importance sampling (IS) weights,
filtering outlier samples via rejection sampling (RS), and
tracking metrics to diagnose and correct off-policy issues.

## Core Capabilities
1. **Multi-Granularity Aggregation**:
   - Importance Sampling (IS):
        Token-level
        Sequence-level
   - Rejection Sampling (RS):
        Divergence-based filters (token_k*, seq_sum_k*, seq_mean_k*, seq_max_k*)
2. **Memory-Efficient Design**:
   - Log-space computations to avoid numerical overflow/underflow.
   - Fixed safety bounds (exp(±20)) for stable exponentiation.
   - Metrics calculated without large intermediate tensors (prevents CUDA OOM).
3. **Comprehensive Metrics Tracking**:
   - IS/RS statistics (mean/max/min, effective sample size ESS, rejection rate).
   - Off-policy diagnostics (KL divergence, perplexity PPL, log PPL difference, χ² divergence).
   - Sequence-level breakdowns (deviation from ideal weights, outlier fraction).

## Key Interfaces & Usage
- compute_rollout_correction_and_rejection_mask(): compute IS weights + rejection mask.
- compute_rollout_correction_weights(): only compute truncated IS weights (for variance
  reduction, no outlier rejection).
- compute_rollout_rejection_mask(): only filter outliers (for sample cleaning, no IS weight
  computation).
- compute_offpolicy_metrics(): called by core functions to calculate off-policy diagnostics
  (KL/PPL/χ²) — no direct external calls needed.

### Integration Notes
- Used in `ray_trainer.py` via `compute_rollout_correction_and_add_to_batch()` (batch training pipeline).
- Used in `dp_actor.py` for distributed worker computations (distributed training scenarios).
- All functions support batch inputs and valid token masking (via `response_mask`).

- "When Speed Kills Stability: Demystifying RL Collapse from the Training-Inference Mismatch": https://richardli.xyz/rl-collapse
- Off-policy RL (theoretical basis for IS): https://fengyao.notion.site/off-policy-rl

steps.reasoning_content:

def fsdp_merge_unmerge(module: nn.Module, do_merge: bool):
    """Merge or unmerge LoRA adapters in FSDP module.

    For FSDP (v1), it gathers all model parameters to each device, which may cause OOM.
    For FSDP2, it gathers model parameters layer-by-layer to reduce memory footprint.

    Args:
        module: The FSDP module to merge/unmerge LoRA adapters
        do_merge: If True, merge LoRA into base model; if False, unmerge LoRA
    """
    version = fsdp_version(module)
    assert version in [1, 2], f"fsdp_merge_unmerge requires FSDP module, got version {version}"

    if version == 1:
        # Unshard → merge → Reshard
        with FSDP.summon_full_params(module, writeback=True, with_grads=False):
            _merge_or_unmerge_lora_(module, merge=do_merge)
    else:
        # FSDP2: Unshard → merge → Reshard layer-by-layer
        for name, submodule in module.named_modules():
            if isinstance(submodule, FSDPModule) and name != "":  # skip root model
                with FSDP.summon_full_params(submodule, writeback=True, with_grads=False):
                    _merge_or_unmerge_lora_(submodule, merge=do_merge)

    Sending LoRA delta keys to these backends fails with KeyError.

    1. Merges LoRA adapters into base weights (layer-by-layer for FSDP2)
    2. Extracts the full merged state dict with clean HF key names

    """Backup base model weights to CPU with LoRA temporarily disabled.

    with torch.no_grad():

But the symptom of training_ppl explosion might be due to FSDP2 LoRA merge corrupting base weights. Let's check `restore_base_model_weights`: it iterates `module.named_parameters()` and copies backup entries by name. `backup_base_model_weights` was called on `actor` — self.module, which for FSDP2 may be the FSDPModule wrapping the PeftModel. `isinstance(module, PeftModel)` — the FSDP2 module wraps... hmm.

Wait. But there's a subtle thing in get_per_tensor_param: `_is_peft = hasattr(getattr(self.module, "_fsdp_wrapped_module", self.module), "peft_config")`. For FSDP2, the module is likely FSDPModule wrapping the actor model (which might be a PEFT model). OK.

But big issue: after `merged_lora_context`, the returned `params = self.module.state_dict()` is a live reference to state dict tensors? state_dict returns references to the model's parameters (not clones) in PyTorch. Then, when exiting the context manager, restore_base_model_weights copies backup weights back into `param.data` — in place! Since state_dict tensors are the same storage as the model params, the restored (unmerged) weights would overwrite the merged values in `params` before/as the generator sends items! But wait: the state dict references are captured, then the context exits immediately after collecting `params` (before the generator is consumed, since `params` ordered dict is built inside the with block but iteration happens outside). Hold on:

```

    params = self.module.state_dict()
    params = normalize_peft_param_name(params)
# exit -> restore base weights in place, overwriting tensors referenced by params?
```

If `state_dict()` returns tensors sharing storage with params, then restore in place corrupts the captured merged tensors. But actually PyTorch state_dict returns the actual param tensors (detached references, same storage). `.copy_()` in place would then modify them. So the "merged" weights sent to vLLM would become the unmerged base weights! That would mean vLLM never gets LoRA updates... but the training side has LoRA. Then the two would diverge: training model (base+LoRA) vs rollout (base only). And training_ppl vs rollout_ppl: which side is more likely to have generated the tokens? The tokens were generated by vLLM with base-only weights (if sync broken). Then training log probs with base+LoRA would be a bit different but not enormous. And there's `base_sync_done=True` and `peft_config=None` so vLLM thinks no LoRA.

Actually wait — the code then does `per_tensor_param` generator that calls `.full_tensor()` on DTensor params. state_dict of FSDP2 returns DTensors that reference shards, and the restore copies CPU backups into param.data. If storage is shared, then yes captured DTensors reflect restored base. Hmm, but `_skip_staging` etc.

For FSDP2, params are DTensors; `.data.copy_` works on local shard? Should.

But here's a critical thing: `backup_base_model_weights` checks `isinstance(module, PeftModel)`. In merged_lora_context, called with self.module (the outer FSDP module? or the model?). If it's not a PeftModel, it backs up ALL parameters except "lora" — including non-LoRA base. That's fine. If it is PeftModel, uses `disable_adapter()` and backs up non-lora params. Fine.

import json, re, statistics
for p in ['outputs/rollouts/1.jsonl','outputs/rollouts/30.jsonl','outputs/rollouts/60.jsonl','outputs/val_generations/0.jsonl','outputs/val_generations/30.jsonl','outputs/val_generations/60.jsonl']:
    rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open(p)]
    n=len(rows)
    lens=[len(r['output']) for r in rows]
    has_h=[('####' in r['output']) for r in rows]
    box=[('\\boxed' in r['output']) for r in rows]
    scores=[r['score'] for r in rows]
    # outputs that are exactly #### number
    bare=sum(1 for r in rows if re.fullmatch(r'\s*####\s*-?[\d.,]+\s*', r['output']))
    print(p, 'n',n, 'meanlen %.1f'%statistics.mean(lens), 'medlen',statistics.median(lens),
          'has#### %.3f'%(sum(has_h)/n), 'boxed %.3f'%(sum(box)/n), 'bare %.3f'%(bare/n),
          'score mean %.4f'%(statistics.mean(scores)), 'score>0', sum(1 for s in scores if s>0))
    # first 5 texts short
    print('  first outputs:', [r['output'][:60].replace('\n','\\n') for r in rows[:5]])
EOF

Interesting. Rollout outputs have mean length 896, median 812 — plausible CoT. Has "####" 34.7% but score mean only 0.126. So of those with ####, maybe 36% correct. So the reward works (exact match final answer), but the model rarely produces ####. Validation: only 17.4% contain ####, score mean 0.0857 (i.e., of the 17.4%, about half are correct). So the model's zero-shot GSM8K accuracy under this strict format is 8.6%, but semantic accuracy with \boxed answers might be ~70%? Let's compute semantic answer correctness using \boxed extraction to see the model's true capability. If true accuracy is ~70% but reward-based accuracy is 8.6%, the reward function is the main defect: it incentivizes format rather than correctness, and the model is being trained on a very sparse/misaligned reward. But is this "unhealthy"? The final val accuracy 8.4%, no improvement. Training reward stuck ~10-16%. Entropy collapse to 0.054. The model is degrading in terms of format? Hmm.

But wait, the task hint "verl_lora_merge_base_weight_sync" strongly points elsewhere. Let me not jump. Let's inspect the whole story.

Important clue: `data.truncation=error` and `data.filter_overlong_prompts=True` — fine.

Another clue: the reward function in verl's gsm8k.py. Let me inspect the workspace's version. Maybe the ground truth extraction strips something. And the data. Let's check the parquet contents: maybe the `answer` field has been corrupted such that only a fraction of examples parse correctly, or `reward_model.ground_truth` wrong. In verl's gsm8k preprocess, data has `answer` field with "#### N" and reward_model ground_truth = answer.split("####")[1].strip(). Let me check the parquet and how many ground truths are valid.

Also check the raw gsm8k vs prepared parquet to see if data processing was tampered.

import re

_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS = 300


def extract_solution(solution_str, method="strict"):
    assert method in ["strict", "flexible"]

    # Optimization: Regular expression matching on very long strings can be slow.
    # For math problems, the final answer is usually at the end.
    # We only match on the last 300 characters, which is a safe approximation for 300 tokens.
    if len(solution_str) > _SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:
        solution_str = solution_str[-_SOLUTION_CLIP_CHARS:]

    if method == "strict":
        # this also tests the formatting of the model
        solutions = re.findall("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        if len(solutions) == 0:
            final_answer = None
        else:
            # take the last solution
            final_answer = solutions[-1].replace(",", "").replace("$", "")
    elif method == "flexible":
        answer = re.findall("(\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
        final_answer = None
        if len(answer) == 0:
            # no reward is there is no answer
            pass
        else:
            invalid_str = ["", "."]
            # find the last number that is not '.'
            for final_answer in reversed(answer):
                if final_answer not in invalid_str:
                    break
    return final_answer


def compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0):
    """The scoring function for GSM8k.

    Reference: Trung, Luong, et al. "Reft: Reasoning with reinforced fine-tuning." Proceedings of the 62nd Annual
    Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2024.

    Args:
        solution_str: the solution text
        ground_truth: the ground truth
        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
        format_score: the score for the format
        score: the score for the correct answer
    """
    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str, method=method)
    if answer is None:
        return 0
    else:
        if answer == ground_truth:
            return score
        else:
            return format_score

def compute_score(solution_str, ground_truth, method="strict", format_score=0.0, score=1.0):
    """The scoring function for GSM8k.

    Reference: Trung, Luong, et al. "Reft: Reasoning with reinforced fine-tuning." Proceedings of the 62nd Annual
    Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers). 2024.

    Args:
        solution_str: the solution text
        ground_truth: the ground truth
        method: the method to extract the solution, choices are 'strict' and 'flexible'
        format_score: the score for the format
        score: the score for the correct answer
    """
    answer = extract_solution(solution_str=solution_str, method=method)
    if answer is None:

    else:
        if answer == ground_truth:
            return score
        else:

import logging

import torch

from verl.protocol import DataProto

logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)


def calculate_token_list_diff(tensor1: torch.Tensor, tensor2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # verify inputs
    if tensor1.numel() == 0 or tensor2.numel() == 0:
        return torch.zeros(tensor1.shape[0], dtype=torch.long, device=tensor1.device)
    if tensor1.shape != tensor2.shape or mask.shape != tensor1.shape or mask.shape != tensor2.shape:
        print(
            f"<WARN> dim of tensor1, tensor2, mask is not equal, {(tensor1.shape)=},{(tensor2.shape)=}, {(mask.shape)=}"
        )
        return torch.ones_like(tensor1)
    # transfer to same device
    if tensor2.device != tensor1.device:
        tensor2 = tensor2.to(tensor1.device)
    if mask.device != tensor1.device:
        mask = mask.to(tensor1.device)

    # calculate diff
    diff_mask = tensor1 != tensor2

    valid_diff_mask = diff_mask & (mask == 1)

    diff_counts = valid_diff_mask.sum(dim=1)

    return diff_counts


def pearson_correlation_coefficient(tensor1: torch.Tensor, tensor2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # implemention of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13585
    if tensor1.shape != tensor2.shape or mask.shape != tensor1.shape or mask.shape != tensor2.shape:
        return 0
    mt1 = torch.masked_select(tensor1, mask)
    mt2 = torch.masked_select(tensor2, mask)
    result = torch.corrcoef(torch.stack([mt1, mt2], dim=0))
    return result[0][1].detach().item()


def calculate_log_prob_diff(log_probs1: torch.Tensor, log_probs2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    full_diff = torch.abs(log_probs1 - log_probs2)
    return torch.masked_select(full_diff, mask)


def calculate_debug_metrics(data: DataProto) -> dict:
    """
    calculate rollout vs actor logprobs diff, for debugging purpose

    Args:
        data: DataProto
            the data batch to calculate
            rollout_log_probs: log_probs record when rollout forward tokens
            old_log_probs(actor log probs): log_probs record when actor forward tokens
            loss_mask or attention_mask: to mask unrelated token
            responses: the response tokens, for calculating size
    Returns:
        dict: metrics
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1->input is valid, 0->input is invalid
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": max value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": mean value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": std value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": logprob's pearson corrcoef of rollout vs. actor, reference to https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13585
    """

    rollout_old_log_probs = data.batch["rollout_log_probs"]
    actor_old_log_probs = data.batch["old_log_probs"]
    if "response_mask" in data.batch:
        logger.debug("response mask found, use it to mask log probs")
        log_prob_mask = data.batch["response_mask"]
    elif "attention_mask" in data.batch:
        log_prob_mask = data.batch["attention_mask"]
    else:
        logger.warning(f"no mask info found, use all log probs, {(data.batch.keys())=}")
        log_prob_mask = torch.ones_like(rollout_old_log_probs)
    responses = data.batch["responses"]
    response_length = responses.size(1)

    response_mask = log_prob_mask[:, -response_length:]
    # calculate pearson corrcoef
    actor_probs = torch.exp(actor_old_log_probs)
    rollout_probs = torch.exp(rollout_old_log_probs)
    response_mask_bool = response_mask.bool()

    # check if there are any valid tokens before computing metrics
    if not response_mask_bool.any():
        logger.warning("response_mask is all False, returning default metrics")
        return {
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 0,
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": float("nan"),
        }

    pearson_corrcoef = pearson_correlation_coefficient(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
    rollout_probs_diff = calculate_log_prob_diff(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
    return {
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1,
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": torch.max(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": torch.mean(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": torch.std(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": pearson_corrcoef,
    }

import torch

from verl.protocol import DataProto

logger = logging.getLogger(__file__)


def calculate_token_list_diff(tensor1: torch.Tensor, tensor2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # verify inputs
    if tensor1.numel() == 0 or tensor2.numel() == 0:
        return torch.zeros(tensor1.shape[0], dtype=torch.long, device=tensor1.device)
    if tensor1.shape != tensor2.shape or mask.shape != tensor1.shape or mask.shape != tensor2.shape:
        print(
            f"<WARN> dim of tensor1, tensor2, mask is not equal, {(tensor1.shape)=},{(tensor2.shape)=}, {(mask.shape)=}"
        )
        return torch.ones_like(tensor1)
    # transfer to same device
    if tensor2.device != tensor1.device:
        tensor2 = tensor2.to(tensor1.device)
    if mask.device != tensor1.device:
        mask = mask.to(tensor1.device)

    # calculate diff
    diff_mask = tensor1 != tensor2

    valid_diff_mask = diff_mask & (mask == 1)

    diff_counts = valid_diff_mask.sum(dim=1)

    return diff_counts


def pearson_correlation_coefficient(tensor1: torch.Tensor, tensor2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # implemention of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13585
    if tensor1.shape != tensor2.shape or mask.shape != tensor1.shape or mask.shape != tensor2.shape:
        return 0
    mt1 = torch.masked_select(tensor1, mask)
    mt2 = torch.masked_select(tensor2, mask)
    result = torch.corrcoef(torch.stack([mt1, mt2], dim=0))
    return result[0][1].detach().item()


def calculate_log_prob_diff(log_probs1: torch.Tensor, log_probs2: torch.Tensor, mask: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    full_diff = torch.abs(log_probs1 - log_probs2)
    return torch.masked_select(full_diff, mask)


def calculate_debug_metrics(data: DataProto) -> dict:
    """
    calculate rollout vs actor logprobs diff, for debugging purpose

    Args:
        data: DataProto
            the data batch to calculate
            rollout_log_probs: log_probs record when rollout forward tokens
            old_log_probs(actor log probs): log_probs record when actor forward tokens
            loss_mask or attention_mask: to mask unrelated token
            responses: the response tokens, for calculating size
    Returns:
        dict: metrics
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1->input is valid, 0->input is invalid
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": max value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": mean value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": std value of logprob diff of rollout vs. actor
            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": logprob's pearson corrcoef of rollout vs. actor, reference to https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.13585
    """

    rollout_old_log_probs = data.batch["rollout_log_probs"]
    actor_old_log_probs = data.batch["old_log_probs"]
    if "response_mask" in data.batch:
        logger.debug("response mask found, use it to mask log probs")
        log_prob_mask = data.batch["response_mask"]
    elif "attention_mask" in data.batch:
        log_prob_mask = data.batch["attention_mask"]
    else:
        logger.warning(f"no mask info found, use all log probs, {(data.batch.keys())=}")
        log_prob_mask = torch.ones_like(rollout_old_log_probs)
    responses = data.batch["responses"]
    response_length = responses.size(1)

    response_mask = log_prob_mask[:, -response_length:]
    # calculate pearson corrcoef
    actor_probs = torch.exp(actor_old_log_probs)
    rollout_probs = torch.exp(rollout_old_log_probs)
    response_mask_bool = response_mask.bool()

    # check if there are any valid tokens before computing metrics
    if not response_mask_bool.any():
        logger.warning("response_mask is all False, returning default metrics")
        return {
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 0,
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": float("nan"),
            "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": float("nan"),
        }

    pearson_corrcoef = pearson_correlation_coefficient(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
    rollout_probs_diff = calculate_log_prob_diff(actor_probs, rollout_probs, response_mask_bool)
    return {
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_valid": 1,
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_max": torch.max(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_mean": torch.mean(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_probs_diff_std": torch.std(rollout_probs_diff).detach().item(),
        "training/rollout_actor_probs_pearson_corr": pearson_corrcoef,
    }

def _test_merged_lora_context_worker(
    rank, world_size, rendezvous_file, strategy, model_config, lora_config_dict, backup_adapters
):
    """Worker function for testing merged_lora_context with FSDP.

    Args:
        rank: Process rank
        world_size: Total number of processes
        rendezvous_file: Path to rendezvous file for distributed init
        strategy: FSDP strategy ("fsdp" or "fsdp2")
        model_config: Model configuration object (Qwen2Config, GptOssConfig, etc.)
        lora_config_dict: Dictionary of LoRA configuration parameters
        backup_adapters: Whether to backup adapter weights before merging
    """
    get_torch_device().set_device(rank)
    torch.distributed.init_process_group(
        backend=get_nccl_backend(),
        init_method=f"file://{rendezvous_file}",
        rank=rank,
        world_size=world_size,
    )
    device_mesh = init_device_mesh(get_device_name(), mesh_shape=(world_size,), mesh_dim_names=("dp",))

    # Create model from provided config
    with torch.device(get_device_name()):
        model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(
            config=model_config, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, attn_implementation="eager"
        )
        model = model.to(device=get_device_name())

    # Add LoRA with provided config
    lora_config = LoraConfig(**lora_config_dict)
    model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)

    # Initialize LoRA adapter weights to non-zero values for testing
    from peft.tuners.lora import LoraLayer

    with torch.no_grad():
        for name, module in model.named_modules():
            if isinstance(module, LoraLayer):
                for adapter_name in module.lora_A.keys():
                    if adapter_name in module.lora_A:
                        # Initialize lora_A with values around 1.0
                        module.lora_A[adapter_name].weight.data.uniform_(0.5, 1.5)
                    if adapter_name in module.lora_B:
                        # Initialize lora_B with values around 2.0
                        module.lora_B[adapter_name].weight.data.uniform_(1.5, 2.5)

    # Wrap model with FSDP
    if strategy == "fsdp":
        mixed_precision = MixedPrecision(
            param_dtype=torch.bfloat16, reduce_dtype=torch.float32, buffer_dtype=torch.float32
        )
        model = FSDP(
            model,
            use_orig_params=True,
            device_id=get_torch_device().current_device(),
            sharding_strategy=ShardingStrategy.FULL_SHARD,
            mixed_precision=mixed_precision,
            device_mesh=device_mesh,
            auto_wrap_policy=get_fsdp_wrap_policy(module=model, is_lora=True),
        )
    else:
        mp_policy = MixedPrecisionPolicy(
            param_dtype=torch.bfloat16, reduce_dtype=torch.float32, cast_forward_inputs=True
        )
        fsdp_kwargs = {
            "mesh": device_mesh,
            "mp_policy": mp_policy,
        }
        apply_fsdp2(model, fsdp_kwargs, {})

    # Test: backup adapter weights, merge, restore
    from peft.tuners.lora import LoraLayer

    lora_layers = [m for m in model.modules() if isinstance(m, LoraLayer)]

    # Verify LoRA layers exist
    assert len(lora_layers) > 0, "Model should have LoRA layers"

    # Initially not merged
    for layer in lora_layers:
        assert not getattr(layer, "merged", False), "LoRA should not be merged initially"

    # Backup adapter weights before merge
    from peft.utils.save_and_load import get_peft_model_state_dict

    original_adapter_weights = get_peft_model_state_dict(model)

    # Use merged_lora_context with the specified backup_adapters flag
    for _ in range(3):
        with merged_lora_context(model, backup_adapters=backup_adapters):
            # Inside context, LoRA should be merged
            for layer in lora_layers:
                assert getattr(layer, "merged", False), "LoRA should be merged inside context"

    # After context, check the state based on backup_adapters flag
    for layer in lora_layers:
        assert not getattr(layer, "merged", False), "LoRA should be unmerged after context"

    restored_adapter_weights = get_peft_model_state_dict(model)

    # Verify adapter weights are restored exactly
    for key in original_adapter_weights.keys():
        assert key in restored_adapter_weights, f"Key {key} should be in restored weights"
        torch.testing.assert_close(
            original_adapter_weights[key].cpu(),
            restored_adapter_weights[key].cpu(),
            rtol=1e-5,
            atol=1e-6,
            msg=f"Adapter weight {key} should be restored to original value",
        )

    if rank == 0:
        model_name = model_config.__class__.__name__
        backup_mode = "with backup" if backup_adapters else "without backup"
        print(f"merged_lora_context test with {model_name} {strategy} {backup_mode} passed on {world_size} GPUs!")

    torch.distributed.barrier()
    torch.distributed.destroy_process_group()

    # Create Qwen2 model config
    model_config = Qwen2Config(num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=2, hidden_size=128)

    # Create LoRA config for Qwen2
    lora_config_dict = {
        "r": 8,
        "lora_alpha": 16,
        "target_modules": ["q_proj", "v_proj"],
        "lora_dropout": 0.0,
        "bias": "none",
        "task_type": "CAUSAL_LM",

        fn=_test_merged_lora_context_worker,
        args=(world_size, rendezvous_file, strategy, model_config, lora_config_dict, backup_adapters),
        nprocs=world_size,

Let's approach from behavior. We have concrete evidence:

1. Base model val accuracy (strict ####) 8.6% at step 0, and remains ~8% through step 60. In fact, semantic accuracy ~28% (boxed or hash). No improvement across 60 steps of GRPO despite training reward ~10-16%.

2. training rollout score ~0.10-0.16 across steps — no upward trend; final lower. Entropy collapses from 0.42 to 0.054. grad_norm grows to ~13-20. Old log probs diverge catastrophically from rollout (training_ppl inf, KL 81).

3. Rollout dump shows outputs often bare "#### number" with no reasoning; but has #### only ~35%. This looks like reward hacking or model collapse.

4. Rollout_corr metrics indicate training/rollout mismatch growing exponentially — the actor and rollout models diverge.

Now the key: is the training/rollout mismatch a cause or consequence? If policy collapse causes entropy low and extreme log probs, then training_ppl computed on sampled tokens can explode because the actor assigns tiny probs to vLLM samples. But both actor and vLLM are synced every step; they should be the same model. A growing mismatch means the weights synced to vLLM differ from the actor's weights. class LoraLayer(BaseTunerLayer):
    # All names of layers that may contain (trainable) adapter weights
    adapter_layer_names: tuple[str, ...] = ("lora_A", "lora_B", "lora_embedding_A", "lora_embedding_B")
    # All names of other parameters that may contain adapter-related parameters
    other_param_names: tuple[str, ...] = ("r", "lora_alpha", "scaling", "lora_dropout")

    def __init__(self, base_layer: nn.Module, ephemeral_gpu_offload: bool = False, **kwargs) -> None:
        self.base_layer = base_layer
        self.r = {}
        self.lora_alpha = {}
        self.scaling = {}
        self.lora_dropout = nn.ModuleDict({})
        self.lora_A = nn.ModuleDict({})
        self.lora_B = nn.ModuleDict({})
        # For Embedding layer
        self.lora_embedding_A = nn.ParameterDict({})
        self.lora_embedding_B = nn.ParameterDict({})
        # Mark the weight as unmerged
        self._disable_adapters = False
        self.merged_adapters = []
        self.use_dora: dict[str, bool] = {}  # not actively used anymore after #2443, keep it for BC
        self.use_rslora: dict[str, bool] = {}
        self.lora_bias: dict[str, bool] = {}
        self.lora_magnitude_vector = torch.nn.ModuleDict()  # for DoRA
        self._caches: dict[str, Any] = {}
        self.ephemeral_gpu_offload: bool = ephemeral_gpu_offload
        # flag to enable/disable casting of input to weight dtype during forward call
        self.cast_input_dtype_enabled: bool = True
        self.lora_variant: dict[str, LoraVariant] = {}
        self.kwargs = kwargs

        base_layer = self.get_base_layer()
        in_features, out_features = _get_in_out_features(base_layer)
        self.in_features = in_features
        self.out_features = out_features

    def resolve_lora_variant(self, *, use_dora: bool, **kwargs) -> Optional[LoraVariant]:
        """Return a matching LoRA variant for this layer type.

        Given the init arguments of this layer, return the correct LoRA variant, if any. E.g., if `use_dora=True`, this
        method should return the DoRA variant for the given layer. If `use_alora=True`, same for aLoRA.

        If there is no fitting variant, return None.

        Note: If this layer type does not support the LoRA variant at all, please raise an error during __init__ as is
        convention, and not here.

        """
        return None

    def update_layer(
        self,
        adapter_name,
        r,
        lora_alpha,
        lora_dropout,
        init_lora_weights,
        use_rslora,
        use_dora: bool = False,
        use_alora: bool = False,
        use_qalora: bool = False,
        lora_bias: bool = False,
        arrow_config: ArrowConfig = None,
        qalora_group_size: int = 32,
        inference_mode: bool = False,
        **kwargs,

        kwargs = locals().copy()
        del kwargs["self"]

        if r <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"`r` should be a positive integer value but the value passed is {r}")

        if lora_bias and (getattr(self.get_base_layer(), "bias", None) is None):

                PeftWarning,

            use_dora=use_dora,
            use_alora=use_alora,
            use_qalora=use_qalora,
            qalora_group_size=qalora_group_size,
            arrow_config=arrow_config,
        )
        if lora_variant is not None:
            self.lora_variant[adapter_name] = lora_variant

        self.r[adapter_name] = r
        self.lora_alpha[adapter_name] = lora_alpha
        if lora_dropout > 0.0:
            lora_dropout_layer = nn.Dropout(p=lora_dropout)
        else:
            lora_dropout_layer = nn.Identity()

        self.lora_dropout.update(nn.ModuleDict({adapter_name: lora_dropout_layer}))

        self.lora_A[adapter_name] = nn.Linear(self.in_features, r, bias=False)
        self.lora_B[adapter_name] = nn.Linear(r, self.out_features, bias=lora_bias)
        self.lora_bias[adapter_name] = lora_bias

        if use_rslora:
            self.scaling[adapter_name] = lora_alpha / math.sqrt(r)
        else:
            self.scaling[adapter_name] = lora_alpha / r

        self.use_rslora[adapter_name] = use_rslora

        self.use_dora[adapter_name] = use_dora

        # for inits that require access to the base weight, use gather_param_ctx so that the weight is gathered when using DeepSpeed
        if isinstance(init_lora_weights, str) and init_lora_weights.startswith("pissa"):
            with gather_params_ctx(self.get_base_layer().weight):
                self.pissa_init(adapter_name, init_lora_weights)
        elif isinstance(init_lora_weights, str) and init_lora_weights.startswith("corda"):
            with gather_params_ctx(self.get_base_layer().weight):
                self.corda_init(adapter_name, init_lora_weights)
        elif isinstance(init_lora_weights, str) and init_lora_weights.lower() == "olora":
            with gather_params_ctx(self.get_base_layer().weight):
                self.olora_init(adapter_name)
        elif init_lora_weights == "loftq":
            with gather_params_ctx(self.get_base_layer().weight):
                self.loftq_init(adapter_name)
        elif init_lora_weights == "eva":
            nn.init.zeros_(self.lora_B[adapter_name].weight)
        elif init_lora_weights == "orthogonal":
            with gather_params_ctx(self.get_base_layer().weight):
                self.orthogonal_init(adapter_name)
        elif init_lora_weights:
            self.reset_lora_parameters(adapter_name, init_lora_weights)
        # call this before init of the lora variants
        self._move_ad

            for active_adapter in self.active_adapters:

                lora_B = self.lora_B[active_adapter]

import sys, pandas as pd, torch

So base model accuracy under strict #### ~8.6%; semantic accuracy ~28%. Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct is genuinely not great here due to format + verbosity? Hmm, but my local generations did not produce #### either (bold answer). The prompt asks #### but model ignores it. The training should teach it. After 60 steps, still ~8.4% val.

So the main issue could be: the training signal is extremely sparse because the reward only counts exact final answer after "####", and the model doesn't produce the format. But over 60 steps × 1024 = 61k samples, it should learn format. Yet entropy collapsed to 0.054 and no accuracy improvement — the policy instead collapsed toward some degenerate behavior.

Now let's examine the actual optimization: GRPO advantage. The rewards are binary 0/1, with mean ~0.12. In a group of 8 samples per prompt, how often is there variance? If most prompts yield all-zero (no #### or all incorrect) and a few all-one, then advantage is zero for most groups. Only ~12% of samples reward>0; probability that a group of 8 has at least one correct varies. Let's estimate: if per-prompt probability of at least one correct is maybe 40%, then only those contribute. Still should learn.

def monkey_patch_compute_logits(model, vocab_size: int, banned_token_ids: Optional[list[int]] = None):
    """Mask the tokens the sampler must never pick.

    Beyond the out-of-vocabulary tail, `banned_token_ids` covers tokens that live *inside* the
    vocabulary yet are still illegal to generate: the vision placeholders, which are meaningless
    unless a real image or video sits behind them. See `get_vision_placeholder_token_ids`.
    """
    original_compute_logits = model.compute_logits

    def compute_logits(
        self,
        *args,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        logits = original_compute_logits(*args, **kwargs)
        logits[..., vocab_size:] = float("-inf")
        if banned_token_ids:
            logits[..., banned_token_ids] = float("-inf")
        return logits

    model.compute_logits = MethodType(compute_logits, model)

As Δ grows, log π_actor(tokens from W0) becomes very low (because the actor has moved to a different distribution), giving training_ppl → inf, kl(rollout||training) huge. Yes.

The actor's entropy: evaluated under its own forward on *rollout* sequences. The actor is trained with GRPO on rewards computed from base-model samples. Because the actor's output distribution diverges from base, and because rewards are nearly always 0/1 with mean 0.1, the policy gradient pushes the actor toward tokens in successful sequences. Entropy drops. The actor's KL to the ref model grows dramatically. The actor may indeed collapse, while its samples are never used (rollout always base). If training samples from the frozen base have ~10-13% reward, the actor learns to imitate/boost successful base trajectories. Actually this could improve actor's greedy accuracy if we evaluated the merged actor... but validation uses vLLM (base), so we never see it. Wait, but is the training reward itself flat? critic/score/mean 0.126 → 0.102. If the actor's learning doesn't affect rollout generation, the training reward stays that of the base model. Yes — generation is base, so reward distribution constant. The small fluctuations are sampling noise and different prompt batches.   - Adapter mode (peft_merge=False): base weights first, then adapter deltas
  - Merge mode (peft_merge=True): single sync with merged weights
  - Non-LoRA: single sync, standard weights

These tests mock the actor engine and rollout to verify call ordering and
arguments without requiring GPU, ray, or sglang infrastructure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, call

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: simulate engine_workers.update_weights() logic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def _update_weights(
    *,
    rollout,
    actor_engine,
    peft_merge: bool,
    base_sync_done: bool,
    free_cache_engine: bool,
    layered_summon: bool = False,
    global_steps: int = None,
    checkpoint_backend: str = "naive",
):
    """Reproduce the update_weights() logic from engine_workers.py.

    This mirrors the actual code so we can test the branching without
    importing the real class (which requires ray, torch, etc.).
    """
    # 0. early return for non-naive checkpoint backend
    if checkpoint_backend != "naive":
        per_tensor_param, _ = actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param()
        return

    # 1. resume weights (conditional on sleep_level)
    if free_cache_engine:
        if getattr(rollout, "sleep_level", 2) != 1:
            await rollout.resume(tags=["weights"])

    # 2. probe adapter-mode params first so we can discover peft_config
    per_tensor_param, peft_config = actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param(
        layered_summon=layered_summon, base_sync_done=True
    )

    # 3. determine base sync need
    do_lora_base_sync = False
    if not peft_merge and peft_config is not None:
        rollout.sleep_level = 1
        do_lora_base_sync = not base_sync_done

    # 4. sync weights
    if do_lora_base_sync:
        per_tensor_param_base, peft_config = actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param(
            layered_summon=layered_summon, base_sync_done=False
        )
        await rollout.update_weights(
            per_tensor_param_base, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=False, global_steps=global_steps
        )

    await rollout.update_weights(
        per_tensor_param, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=True, global_steps=global_steps
    )

    # 5. resume kv_cache
    if free_cache_engine:
        await rollout.resume(tags=["kv_cache"])


def _make_mocks(peft_config=None, params_by_base_sync_done=None):
    """Create mock rollout and actor engine.

    Args:
        peft_config: If not None, get_per_tensor_param returns this as peft_config.
            Use a truthy value (e.g. MagicMock()) for LoRA, None for non-LoRA/merge.
        params_by_base_sync_done: Optional mapping used to return different params
            for probe (`True`) and base sync (`False`) calls.
    """
    rollout = AsyncMock()
    # Don't pre-set sleep_level — let the code set it via getattr default
    del rollout.sleep_level

    if params_by_base_sync_done is None:
        params_by_base_sync_done = {False: "fake_params", True: "fake_params"}

    actor_engine = MagicMock()

    def _get_per_tensor_param(*args, **kwargs):
        base_sync_done = kwargs.get("base_sync_done", True)
        return params_by_base_sync_done[base_sync_done], peft_config

    actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param = MagicMock(side_effect=_get_per_tensor_param)

    return rollout, actor_engine


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Adapter mode tests (peft_merge=False, peft_config is not None)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestAdapterModeFirstIteration:
    """First iteration in adapter mode: base_sync_done=False."""

                base_sync_done=False,

            )
        )

        second_call = rollout.update_weights.call_args_list[1]
        assert first_call.args[0] == "fake_base_params"
        assert second_call.args[0] == "fake_adapter_params"
        assert first_call.kwargs["base_sync_done"] is False
        assert second_call.kwargs["base_sync_done"] is True

    def test_sets_sleep_level_to_1(self):
        """After first iteration, sleep_level should be set to 1."""
        peft_cfg = MagicMock()
        rollout, engine = _make_mocks(peft_config=peft_cfg)

        asyncio.run(
            _update_weights(
                rollout=rollout,
                actor_engine=engine,
                peft_merge=False,
                base_sync_done=False,
                free_cache_engine=True,
            )
        )

        assert rollout.sleep_level == 1

        """First iteration: sleep_level not yet set, so weight resume fires."""
        peft_cfg = MagicMock()
        rollout, engine = _make_mocks(peft_config=peft_cfg)

        asyncio.run(
            _update_weights(
                rollout=rollout,
                actor_engine=engine,
                peft_merge=False,
                base_sync_done=False,
                free_cache_engine=True,
            )
        )

        # resume called twice: weights then kv_cache
        resume_calls = rollout.resume.call_args_list
        assert call(tags=["weights"]) in resume_calls
        assert call(tags=["kv_cache"]) in resume_calls


class TestAdapterModeSubsequentIterations:
    """Subsequent iterations in adapter mode: base_sync_done=True, sleep_level=1."""

    def test_single_update_weights_call(self):
        """Only adapter deltas sent, no base sync."""
        peft_cfg = MagicMock()

        assert rollout.update_weights.call_args.kwargs["base_sync_done"] is True

    def test_skips_weight_resume(self):
        """With sleep_level=1, weight resume is skipped."""
        peft_cfg = MagicMock()
        rollout, engine = _make_mocks(peft_config=peft_cfg)
        rollout.sleep_level = 1

        asyncio.run(
            _update_weights(
                rollout=rollout,
                actor_engine=engine,
                peft_merge=False,
                base_sync_done=True,
                free_cache_engine=True,
            )
        )

        # Only kv_cache resume, no weight resume
        resume_calls = rollout.resume.call_args_list
        assert call(tags=["weights"]) not in resume_calls
        assert call(tags=["kv_cache"]) in resume_calls


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Merge mode tests (peft_merge=True)

"""Unit tests for LoRA weight sync ordering in engine_workers.update_weights().

Tests the branching logic that controls how weights are synced to the rollout:
  - Adapter mode (peft_merge=False): base weights first, then adapter deltas
  - Merge mode (peft_merge=True): single sync with merged weights
  - Non-LoRA: single sync, standard weights

These tests mock the actor engine and rollout to verify call ordering and
arguments without requiring GPU, ray, or sglang infrastructure.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, MagicMock, call

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper: simulate engine_workers.update_weights() logic
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


async def _update_weights(
    *,
    rollout,
    actor_engine,
    peft_merge: bool,
    base_sync_done: bool,
    free_cache_engine: bool,
    layered_summon: bool = False,
    global_steps: int = None,
    checkpoint_backend: str = "naive",
):
    """Reproduce the update_weights() logic from engine_workers.py.

    This mirrors the actual code so we can test the branching without
    importing the real class (which requires ray, torch, etc.).
    """
    # 0. early return for non-naive checkpoint backend
    if checkpoint_backend != "naive":
        per_tensor_param, _ = actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param()
        return

    # 1. resume weights (conditional on sleep_level)
    if free_cache_engine:
        if getattr(rollout, "sleep_level", 2) != 1:
            await rollout.resume(tags=["weights"])

    # 2. probe adapter-mode params first so we can discover peft_config
    per_tensor_param, peft_config = actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param(
        layered_summon=layered_summon, base_sync_done=True
    )

    # 3. determine base sync need
    do_lora_base_sync = False
    if not peft_merge and peft_config is not None:
        rollout.sleep_level = 1
        do_lora_base_sync = not base_sync_done

    # 4. sync weights
    if do_lora_base_sync:
        per_tensor_param_base, peft_config = actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param(
            layered_summon=layered_summon, base_sync_done=False
        )
        await rollout.update_weights(
            per_tensor_param_base, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=False, global_steps=global_steps
        )

    await rollout.update_weights(
        per_tensor_param, peft_config=peft_config, base_sync_done=True, global_steps=global_steps
    )

    # 5. resume kv_cache
    if free_cache_engine:
        await rollout.resume(tags=["kv_cache"])


def _make_mocks(peft_config=None, params_by_base_sync_done=None):
    """Create mock rollout and actor engine.

    Args:
        peft_config: If not None, get_per_tensor_param returns this as peft_config.
            Use a truthy value (e.g. MagicMock()) for LoRA, None for non-LoRA/merge.
        params_by_base_sync_done: Optional mapping used to return different params
            for probe (`True`) and base sync (`False`) calls.
    """
    rollout = AsyncMock()
    # Don't pre-set sleep_level — let the code set it via getattr default
    del rollout.sleep_level

    if params_by_base_sync_done is None:
        params_by_base_sync_done = {False: "fake_params", True: "fake_params"}

    actor_engine = MagicMock()

    def _get_per_tensor_param(*args, **kwargs):
        base_sync_done = kwargs.get("base_sync_done", True)
        return params_by_base_sync_done[base_sync_done], peft_config

    actor_engine.get_per_tensor_param = MagicMock(side_effect=_get_per_tensor_param)

    return rollout, actor_engine

Our experiment already used FSDP2 with root wrapping and showed aliasing. Good.

However, in the real engine, `self.module` could be a `PeftModel` wrapped by FSDP2 root (fully_shard(model)) — our test exactly.

One more check: In our test, did `merged_lora_context` actually merge the correct FSDP2 submodules? The diff inside was 46.5, so yes merged. And after restore, sd == base. Confirmed.

So the mechanism is real and demonstrable.

There's a potential counterargument: maybe in the actual run, `get_per_tensor_param` is called with `base_sync_done=True`, and in the merge branch, they call `self.module.state_dict()` — but perhaps the vLLM `update_weights` consumes the generator *inside* the with block? No; the context manager encloses only state_dict and normalize. The generator expression defined after.

Hold on, let me re-read lines 815-880 carefully. The `with merged_lora_context(...)` block ends before `params = convert_weight_keys(...)`. The generator `per_tensor_param` is defined after. So at consumption, restore has happened. Yes.

But how did this ever pass tests? In the SGLang path, `collect_merged_lora_params` materializes full CPU tensors inside the merge context (`param.full_tensor().detach().cpu()`), so it works. In the FSDP2 `get_per_tensor_param` merge branch, it doesn't materialize inside the context — that's the bug. Perhaps this snapshot is precisely at a commit where the vLLM merge path regressed.

Now, is there evidence in the logs that vLLM receives the base model? Yes:
- Val outputs nearly identical across steps.
- Training rollouts: reward flat.
- Actor-vs-rollout logprob divergence growing.

But wait, there's an even more direct piece of evidence available: the training rollouts at different steps should be generated by the same static base model (if the hypothesis holds). But prompts differ per step, so we can't directly compare. However, we can check if the *distributional statistics* of rollouts are static: mean length, #### rate, boxed rate, score, etc. — all static (see above: nearly constant). Also `rollout_ppl` from vLLM constant ~1.5. And the base model's outputs should have a specific style. We could test: regenerate one prompt that appeared in a rollout dump at step 60 using the base model (greedy vs sampled, T=1, seed?) and see if it matches. Rollouts use n=8 samples with temperature 1.0 and seed 42; vLLM sampling with seed 42 per request? Hard to reproduce exactly.

Another strong check: the `critic/score/mean` per step equals the reward of samples from a frozen model. If the model were improving, reward would trend up. It doesn't.

Now, there's a nuance: the LoRA adapter also receives training; the actor could learn. But evaluation never sees it. Could the benchmark's expected answer be "unhealthy due to LoRA merge weight sync bug causing rollout to train against a frozen base policy"? Likely.

Excellent. Perfectly monotonic divergence of actor vs rollout: rollout_ppl stays ~1.5 (vLLM's own confidence), training_ppl explodes, pearson falls 0.97 → 0.18. Meanwhile reward flat ~0.12-0.15 and response length flat ~270, rollout reward/ppl flat. This is exactly a static rollout policy being scored by a drifting actor.

Now, one more important thing: I should confirm that the *actor* (training) isn't the static one and vLLM the drifting one. Evidence: rollout_ppl (vLLM log probs of its own samples) stays ~1.5 — the generating model is confident in its own outputs, so vLLM is coherent. training_ppl = actor's ppl of the same tokens explodes. If vLLM were the drifting one (receiving corrupted compounded weights), its samples would be increasingly weird, but rollout_ppl could still be low because it's self-consistent. However, val generations would then change progressively; they're static. Also, the actor's entropy collapses — a trained policy can collapse; a corrupted one too. Which model is static? Val outputs static ⇒ vLLM static. If vLLM received weight updates every step and those updates were *literally the unmerged base*, static. If vLLM received corrupted compounded weights, val outputs would change wildly. They don't. So vLLM = static base. Actor drifts (kl to ref grows to 7.8, entropy collapses). This fits aliasing.

Wait, but hold on: actor/kl_loss 7.8 vs ref. If the actor's LoRA training is fed reward from frozen-base rollouts, could the actor really drift that far in 60 steps with lr 3e-5? KL 7.8 nats/token is enormous; entropy 0.05. The LoRA adapter may have blown up because its log-probs on the rollout data are far off-policy, and the PPO ratio clipping... Actually here's a deeper dynamic: PPO/GRPO on samples from a different (frozen) policy with huge importance ratios; old_log_probs computed by the actor at the *current* policy each step (not the generating policy). Wait, how does verl handle this? Rollout generates tokens from vLLM (base). Then `compute_log_prob` computes old_log_probs with the actor (current LoRA policy). So old_log_probs are from the actor's current policy, not the generating policy. The policy gradient then uses these as the "old" policy for the PPO ratio; the actor update uses the same model, so within a step the ratio is ~1 initially. But the *rollout_log_probs* recorded from vLLM reflect the base model. The advantage is computed from rewards of base samples. Training proceeds on off-policy data, but PPO's ratio is actor-new vs actor-old (both current), so no off-policy correction. The actor can drift arbitrarily, since nothing anchors it to the generating policy except the reference KL penalty (coef 0.001, negligible). This leads to exactly the observed: actor drifts far, entropy collapses, KL to ref explodes, while rollouts/rewards stay frozen. Great.

Furthermore, GRPO advantage uses group-normalized rewards of the 8 base-model samples. Since the actor isn't generating them, the learning signal doesn't correspond to its own behavior; the policy may still optimize to produce high-reward continuations. But with kl coef 0.001 and 60 steps, it can drift to a degenerate low-entropy policy that it thinks yields reward — essentially "hallucinated" optimization on another policy's data. Wait, but why should the actor's entropy collapse to 0.05? Because the actor is trained with a PG objective on data it didn't generate; still, the gradient pushes up probabilities of high-reward sequences and down on low-reward ones. As it overfits to the fixed data batches from the base, its distribution sharpens. Plausible.

Now: is the val evaluation (row 0.0857 → 0.0842) from vLLM base? Yes. Note that val accuracy is computed with the strict #### extraction. The base model rarely emits #### (17% in val). So absolute accuracy is low but that's a separate quality issue, not necessarily a defect of the experiment if the reward is intended to teach format. The RL setup itself could work if generation came from the trained model, since training samples already have 35% #### (sampling 8× increases format presence). Over time the actor would learn to emit #### and correct answers; but vLLM never uses it.

Let me now verify whether the run is "healthy" in any other respects:
- Truncation: response_length/clip_ratio ~0.001, no issue. Val has some near-1024 but clip ratio small. Not a defect.
- Runtime: step time ~43s, stable; throughput ~9k tokens/s; no OOM; the tail has a DataLoader worker killed and wandb pipe error at shutdown, likely after final step. Not causal.
- Data: 7473/1319 rows; standard preprocessing; no overlap? Let me check train/test overlap quickly (GSM8K standard splits are disjoint). Could check.
- Reward: strict ####; training reward computed correctly.
- The log at the end shows `training/epoch:1` at step 60 — hmm, epoch 1 at step 60 because 7473/128 = 58.4 epochs... wait, trainer.total_training_steps=60, data.train_batch_size=128, so one epoch = 7473/128 = 58 batches. Step 55 missing in console-history (jump from 54 to 56!) — interesting: step 55 missing. Let's check. The console-history shows steps ... 53, 54, 56, 57... training/epoch 0 until step 54, then 1 at step 56. The missing step 55 could be an anomaly (skipped logging? crash? filter?). Let me investigate train.log around step 55.

Also the log ends with `DataLoader worker (pid 22917) is killed by signal: Killed` — likely memory pressure at shutdown. CPU memory used 499 GB (!) at step 60. Could be an OOM-ish environment, but step times stable.

Let me look at steps 50-60 in train.log to see if something happened (e.g., an epoch boundary, skipped batch due to filtering). Search "step:55".

Confirmed: engine uses apply_fsdp2. And comment at 827 literally says "FSDP2 state_dict() only collects DTensor refs and the generator below already stages each shard lazily via .to(device).full_tensor()" — acknowledging lazy materialization. This makes the in-place restore before consumption definitively corrupt the synced weights. The bug is the interaction of `backup_adapters=True` + lazy materialization.

Now let me also consider: is this the *only* root cause? The task says "root cause or causes". There's also the fact that with merge=True and load_format=dummy, at step 0, vLLM receives base weights (fine). The validation accuracy 8.6% at step 0 is low because the base model doesn't follow the #### format. Not a defect in the experiment per se, but the reward strictness means low reward. Not causal to "no learning" though? Hmm, actually with correct weight sync, would the run be healthy? Let's think.

If weights synced correctly, vLLM would generate from the current merged policy. The training reward would reflect the improved policy. GRPO would then learn. It's plausible.

But is there a secondary issue: `actor_rollout_ref.model.lora.merge=True` is specified without "+", but that's valid. `load_format` default dummy; fine.

What about `actor_rollout_ref.rollout.layered_summon` default False? The upstream example sets layered_summon=True for merge. Not needed for vLLM in-place IPC? layered_summon is used for collect_lora_params? In get_per_tensor_param, layered_summon passed to collect_lora_params only in non-merge path. Merge path ignores it. Not causal.

What about `ref` model with LoRA? The ref is a separate FSDP engine copy of the base model? With LoRA, the ref worker loads base model without adapter; it computes ref log probs for KL loss. That's fine.

What about `actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True` and kl_loss_coef 0.001 — weak anchor, allowing drift. Combined with frozen rollouts, the actor can drift. Not a root cause independent of the sync bug.

Let me also double-check the "training/rollout_probs_diff" metric computation: it compares probs, not log probs, so max diff 1.0 means one model assigns prob 1.0 to a token (very confident) and other assigns 0. At step 60 actor entropy 0.054 could assign prob near 1 for some tokens; base assigns something else. Actually this suggests the *actor* is extremely confident (near-deterministic) on these tokens, while base is not. The actor's old_log_prob for some tokens maybe ~0 (prob 1) and rollout prob different. And training_ppl inf means mean old_log_prob → -inf: actor gives zero probability to some sampled tokens. Yes.
